groups.name: Generative art
groups.about: Artists' systems: rules, randomness and growth that make a picture no one drew by hand.

works.name: Flow Fields
works.context: A technique essay on his blog; Fidenza, his 2021 Art Blocks series, is built on it.
works.picture: Thick curves flowing side by side without touching.
works.math: A grid of angles from Perlin noise; each step moves by (cos a, sin a) times its length. Angles snapped to multiples of π/4 give a fractured look, and collision checks keep the curves apart.

works.name: differential-line
works.context: A personal research repository, archived in 2019.
works.picture: A closed line that folds like coral or brain tissue.
works.math: Nodes repel their neighbors and are pulled toward the two they are linked to; a node is inserted where the curve bends most, and the line never crosses itself.

works.name: hyphae
works.context: A personal research repository.
works.picture: Root- or fungus-like branching networks.
works.math: Branches grow step by step and stop where they would overlap: a branching tree under a no-collision rule.

works.name: sand-spline
works.context: A personal research repository, archived in 2019.
works.picture: Grainy, sand-textured ribbons.
works.math: Splines whose control points drift by noise, drawn as thousands of translucent dots.

works.name: Substrate
works.context: The Machines gallery on complexification.net, his personal Processing experiments.
works.picture: A crystalline network of lines, like a city seen from above.
works.math: Cracks grow straight until they hit another crack, then new ones branch off at right angles; a grid records where cracks are.

works.name: Schotter (Gravel)
works.context: Drawn on a Zuse Graphomat Z64 plotter; Zellyn reconstructed the original ALGOL program in 2024.
works.picture: A 22 by 12 grid of squares that falls into disorder.
works.math: Square i of 264 is shifted by up to ±5·i/264 and rotated by a jitter that grows with i/264: randomness rising in a straight line.

works.name: (Des)Ordres
works.context: Early plotter drawings, ink on paper; the title puns on disorder and orders.
works.picture: Concentric squares in a grid, some missing, some shaken.
works.math: Nested squares in each cell, with random omission and random offsets of their corners.

works.name: Physarum
works.context: A GPU simulation of millions of agents, after Jeff Jones's 2010 model of slime mold.
works.picture: Glowing networks of veins, like slime mold.
works.math: Agents sense the trail ahead, turn toward it and deposit more; the trail map diffuses and decays.

works.name: Looping animations
works.context: Tutorials on his site and 21 commented animations.
works.picture: Seamless loops of Hilbert curves, spirals and spheres.
works.math: Periodic functions of time, a phase offset per object, easing, and noise sampled around a circle so it loops.

works.name: Differential growth and space colonization
works.context: Experiments, with a curated list of morphogenesis resources.
works.picture: Leaf venation and lines that grow and fold.
works.math: Space colonization after Runions et al. (2007): veins grow toward the nearest of many attractor points.

groups.name: Patterns, tilings and rules
groups.about: Tiles, attractors and written instructions: simple local rules with global structure.

works.name: 10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1)); : GOTO 10
works.artist: Nick Montfort, Patsy Baudoin, John Bell, Ian Bogost, Jeremy Douglass, Mark C. Marino, Michael Mateas, Casey Reas, Mark Sample and Noah Vawter
works.context: A book from MIT Press about one line of Commodore 64 BASIC; free as a PDF.
works.picture: An endless random maze of diagonals.
works.math: A coin flip per cell picks / or ; a maze emerges from independent local choices.

works.name: Multi-Scale Truchet Patterns
works.context: A paper at Bridges 2018.
works.picture: Interlocking arcs and lobes at several sizes.
works.math: Quarter-circle arcs between edge midpoints; a tile splits into four at half the size, with winged tiles so the sizes join.

works.name: Tactile
works.context: A library for Escher-like tilings, ported from his C++ version.
works.picture: Interlocking tiles of any shape you draw.
works.math: 81 of the 93 isohedral tiling types, each with 0 to 6 parameters; tiles are placed by affine matrices.

works.name: Penrose Tiling Explained
works.context: A blog post explaining his Python generator.
works.picture: A pattern that never repeats, with fivefold symmetry.
works.math: Two golden triangles, with 36° and 108° apexes, subdivided at golden-ratio points, recursively.

works.name: Clifford attractors
works.artist: Clifford Pickover; page by Paul Bourke
works.context: Paul Bourke's pages on fractals.
works.picture: Silky clouds of millions of points.
works.math: Iterate x' = sin(a·y) + c·cos(a·x), y' = sin(b·x) + d·cos(b·y) and plot every point it lands on.

works.name: Reaction-Diffusion Tutorial
works.context: A tutorial on his site.
works.picture: Spots, stripes and labyrinths like animal coats.
works.math: The Gray-Scott model: two chemicals diffuse at different rates and react, with feed f = 0.055 and kill k = 0.062, over a 3 by 3 Laplacian.

works.name: StippleGen 2
works.context: Made for drawing machines like the Eggbot.
works.picture: A photo redrawn as dots, or as one unbroken line.
works.math: Weighted Voronoi stippling: Lloyd's relaxation moves each dot to the centroid of its cell; the single line is a travelling-salesman tour.

works.name: The ReCode Project
works.context: Recreations of works from the journal Computer Graphics and Art.
works.picture: Early plotter art by Molnár and others.
works.math: Varies by piece: grids, jitter and superposition.

works.name: Solving Sol
works.context: Sol LeWitt's wall drawings were written instructions for others to carry out; this project turns them into programs.
works.picture: Lines and shapes from written rules.
works.math: Each English instruction becomes parameters and a program: an algorithm as a score.

groups.name: Algorithms and math made visible
groups.about: Explanations beautiful enough to be art: sorts, samples, transforms and matrices, drawn.

works.name: Visualizing Algorithms
works.context: An article from his talk at Eyeo 2014.
works.picture: Even-but-random dots, shuffles, sorts and mazes growing.
works.math: Bridson's Poisson-disc sampling, Fisher–Yates against a biased shuffle, quicksort and mergesort, and mazes as random spanning trees (depth-first, Prim's, Wilson's).

works.name: Visualising sorting algorithms
works.context: A blog post arguing for static diagrams over animations.
works.picture: Braided lines, one per element, shaded by value.
works.math: Every swap drawn over time, so a sort's whole history is one picture.

works.name: Portrait of the Hilbert Curve
works.context: A blog post.
works.picture: A Hilbert curve colored by position, and the color cube walked along it.
works.math: Compact Hilbert indices in any number of dimensions; nearby indices land near each other.

works.name: manim and Essence of Linear Algebra
works.context: His own animation tool for his math videos.
works.picture: The whole plane's grid bending under a matrix, the basis vectors riding along.
works.math: Interpolating from the identity to a matrix and applying it to every grid line.

works.name: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues; Markov Chains
works.context: Interactives from Explained Visually.
works.picture: Points pushed along eigen-directions, spiraling for complex eigenvalues; a weather chain hopping between states.
works.math: Repeated matrix–vector products, and powers of a transition matrix settling to a steady state.

works.name: An Interactive Introduction to Fourier Transforms
works.context: A personal explainer.
works.picture: A drawing rebuilt by circles spinning on circles, and JPEG's 8 by 8 cosine images.
works.math: The discrete Fourier transform: each coefficient is one circle's radius, speed and starting angle.

works.name: Drawing with Fourier Transform and Epicycles
works.context: Coding Challenge #130, live-coded on video.
works.picture: Epicycles tracing a path point by point.
works.math: The DFT of the path's points, with the circles chained in order of size.

works.name: SVD image compression
works.context: An interactive demo.
works.picture: A photo sharpening as the rank rises.
works.math: Keeping the k largest singular values: a sum of k rank one layers.

works.name: Hexagonal Grids
works.context: An interactive guide for game developers.
works.picture: Hex grids with rings, lines and rotations.
works.math: Cube coordinates on the plane x + y + z = 0; rotation by permuting coordinates; rounding back to the nearest hex.

works.name: The Book of Shaders
works.artist: Patricio Gonzalez Vivo and Jen Lowe
works.context: An online book about fragment shaders.
works.picture: Fields of color from shaping functions, matrices and noise.
works.math: One function of (x, y) for every pixel, run on the GPU.

groups.name: Turtles and tiny code
groups.about: Communities that make art from very little: a turtle, a formula, 140 characters.

works.name: Turtletoy
works.context: A JavaScript turtle-graphics site for plotter art, with SVG and G-code export.

code.label: Every turtle's source, on the site

works.picture: Line art: differential growth, Fibonacci circles, hexagonal trees, grid waves.
works.math: Forward and turn, with hidden-line tricks for 3D. Each author picks a license; the default is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

works.name: tixy.land
works.context: Creative code golf: 32 characters at most.
works.picture: A grid of dots pulsing in waves, rings and checkerboards.
works.math: One pure function of time, index, x and y gives each dot its size and sign.

works.name: Dwitter
works.context: Launched at the Solskogen demoparty.
works.picture: Whole animations in 140 characters of JavaScript.
works.math: Trigonometry and modular arithmetic folded into one expression per frame.

works.name: Generative Design code package
works.artist: Benedikt Groß, Hartmut Bohnacker, Julia Laub and Claudius Lazzeroni
works.context: Every sketch from the book Generative Design, p5.js edition.
works.picture: Studies in color, shape, type and image.
works.math: Grids, randomness, noise, agents and recursion, one small sketch each.
